subsystems.name: Sensing layer
subsystems.role: detects people, air, sound and objects without anybody touching a device.
parts: millimetre-wave radar and passive infrared occupancy sensors

subsystems.name: Compute and edge layer
subsystems.role: processes sensor data locally so raw footage and audio never leave the room.

subsystems.name: Networking
subsystems.role: connects hundreds of nodes per building without new cabling to each one.
parts: low-power wireless mesh (Thread, Zigbee, Bluetooth mesh)

subsystems.name: Output layer
subsystems.role: presents information on surfaces, in the air or as sound.
parts: laser projectors and waveguides embedded in glass

subsystems.name: Power
subsystems.role: keeps nodes alive for years without maintenance.
parts: indoor photovoltaic, thermal and radio-frequency energy harvesting

subsystems.name: Building integration and control
subsystems.role: ties the mesh to heating, lighting and access systems, and to a digital twin of the building.

buildSteps.title: Fix the interfaces
buildSteps.detail: Agree on data models and radio standards first, so sensors from different makers can join one mesh; without this, the building becomes a set of islands.

buildSteps.title: Make the sensor nodes
buildSteps.detail: Silicon chips with integrated radar or MEMS sensing elements are fabricated, packaged into millimetre-scale modules and tested in volume.

buildSteps.title: Embed them in materials
buildSteps.detail: Nodes, antennas and conductive traces are laminated into ceiling tiles, wall panels, flooring and glass during manufacture, or printed onto flexible substrates that are glued behind finishes.

buildSteps.title: Provide power and backhaul
buildSteps.detail: Each panel gets either a wired Power-over-Ethernet drop or a harvester plus battery sized for a ten-year life; mesh nodes relay to a few wired gateways.

buildSteps.title: Install edge compute
buildSteps.detail: Small servers placed in service cupboards run the inference models and the middleware that turns raw signals into events such as 'room occupied' or 'filter due'.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the output layer
buildSteps.detail: Projectors, waveguide glass and directional speakers are aligned with the surfaces they serve; light-field or true volumetric displays would be built as an array of phase modulators behind the glass — a step that remains laboratory work.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate each space
buildSteps.detail: Every room is walked, measured and tuned so it knows its own geometry, noise floor and normal occupancy pattern.

buildSteps.title: Operate and update
buildSteps.detail: The mesh runs alongside the building-management system, with models retrained as furniture, partitions and usage change over the building's life.

prerequisites.why: the mesh needs thousands of cheap, tiny, low-power detectors rather than a few expensive instruments.
nodes must self-form a network and relay through each other without per-device cabling.
inference must run inside the room at a few watts, not in a distant data centre.
maintenance cost, not hardware cost, kills large sensor deployments.
free-space images that many people can see from any angle in a lit room do not yet exist outside the laboratory.
a mesh that senses everyone continuously is only acceptable if it cannot be turned into surveillance.

pathway.milestone: smart buildings with networked sensors, occupancy-driven lighting and heating, and voice interfaces in the home
pathway.unlocks: the sensing and control groundwork, in partial form.

pathway.milestone: standardised, interoperable mesh at building scale, with most processing on-device
pathway.unlocks: retrofits that work across vendors, and cheaper energy use.

pathway.milestone: displays and controls woven into glass and wall panels in commercial pilot buildings
pathway.unlocks: interfaces that appear where they are needed instead of on a carried screen.

pathway.milestone: true volumetric or light-field output embedded in building materials, with personalised services delivered per person
pathway.unlocks: the screenless environment the concept describes — contingent on the display and privacy problems being solved.
